The petitioners in O.P.(M.V.) No.225/2007on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Irinjalakuda are the appellants herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioners filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Originally the petition was filed by one Vijayan claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 29.3.2006.
During the pendency of the OP, he died and his legal representatives were impleaded as additional petitioners 2 to 5.

According to the petitioner, on 29.3.2003, while he was walking through the eastern side of NH 47 road in front of Appollo Tyres,
Perambra, a Tempo bearing registration No.KL-7 3022 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit him down and as a result of which he sustained injuries.
3. The 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due 2025:KER:10003 to the negligence of the Thulasi vs Varghese on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57769372/
2 driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.1,98,000/-
4.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of documentary evidence Exhibits.A1 to A6, and B1.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.26,100/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioners preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9.

Heard Sri. T.N. Manoj, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri. E.M.
Joseph, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to the petitioner, he was working in Appollo Tyres getting a monthly salary of Rs.12,000/-.

In order to prove the loss of earning, he has produced Exhibit A5 certificate issued by the Associate Manager (HR), Appollo Tyres, stating that the petitioner was on leave from the office during the period from 29.3.2006 to 18.8.2006 and as such he has lost a sum of Rs.63,971.52 towards salary.
It appears that nobody was examined before the Tribunal to prove Exhibit A5, but it was marked without objection.
In such circumstances, I am inclined to accept Exhibit A5 and come to the conclusion that because of the accident, the petitioner sustained a loss of Rs.63,971.52 in his salary.
Therefore, towards loss of earning, he is entitled to get a sum of Rs.63,971.52.

11. In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"fracture 5th rib, fracture D6, acromio clavicular dislocation right side, moderate right pneumotherare, min displaced fracture 5th MC."
He was treated as inpatient for a total period of 24 days.

sentences.text: In this case the petitioner has not produced any disability certificate and as such the petitioner is not entitled to get any compensation on the head 'loss due to disability'.
13. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.12,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.5,000/- was awarded and towards 'bystander expenses' Rs.1,600/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
Towards the head 'extra nourishment', no compensation was awarded.
14. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries including three fractures in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 24 days.

Because of the injuries sustained and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life' and 'bystander expenses' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.30,000/-, Rs.15,000/- and 3,600/- respectively.
For the very same reasons the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.3,000/- on the head 'extra nourishment'.
15. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as 2025:KER:10003 the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
16. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.1,17,072/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

Sl.
 No.
Head of Claim Amount awarded by Amount Awarded in  Tribunal (in Rs.) Appeal(in Rs.)

1 Loss of earning 6,000/- 63,972/-
 2 Bystander expenses 1,600/- 3,600/-
 3 Transportation 1,500/- 1,500/-
 4 Pain and sufferings 12,000/- 30,000/-
 5 Loss of amenities 5,000/- 15,000/-
 6 Extra nourishment Nil 3,000/-
 Total 26,100/- 1,17,072/-
 Enhanced Rs.90,972/-
17.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.1,17,072/- (Rupees One Lakh Seventeen Thousand and Seventy Two Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @
8% per annum from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, excluding interest for a period of 1027 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
2025
On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
